Quick triage notes (summary of first 15 minutes):
- Alert window: 08:38–09:22 PST — system-wide 5xx/429 spike correlated with increased latency for model v8.1-q (quantized profile).
- Error surface: majority of 5xx are downstream timeouts inside the quantized kernel path (serving runtime returning 502/504) and a subset 429s emitted by front-door when KV cache fill throughput exceeded safe limits leading to temporary throttles.
- Impact: RetailCo traffic is routed to our EU+US pool; the spike appears in US nodes where v8.1-q rollouts reached ~60% of traffic at 08:35.

I attached a short log excerpt and the kernel diff we deployed this morning (model_v8.1-quant-diff.patch). Early hypothesis: a kernel change intended to speed mixed-precision matmul introduced a pathological code path for long-context requests, causing stalls and cascade timeouts (retry storm).

Proposed immediate actions (ranked):
1) Hot rollback: pin RetailCo traffic back to v8.0 (float) for the affected routes — fast but requires coordination.
2) Throttle policy: enable short-term request shaping (p99 cutoff at 800ms) to prevent client retries from amplifying.
3) Patch and canary: revert kernel commit in v8.1-q and redeploy to a canary pool after bench tests.

I recommend action 1 + 2 now. I’ll start rollback runbook if we have sign-off.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: model_v8.1-quant-diff.patch

Rollback started at 10:27 PST. Steps executed:
- Updated routing rule for RetailCo -> pinned to model v8.0 on US pool.
- Gradual drain of quantized instances serving RetailCo.
- Enabled shaping policy (p99 cutoff 800ms) for 30 minutes to reduce retry amplification.

Current telemetry (10:36): p95 error rate down from 6.9% to 1.8% on affected routes. Timeouts are trending down; we see p50 latency improving. Attaching recovery heatmap — hotspots around 08:35–09:10 are no longer active.

Next steps: keep RetailCo on v8.0 for 24 hours, run a focused regression test on long-context requests with v8.1-quant diff reverted, and prepare a postmortem with root cause (kernel path for mixed-precision matmul).

— Marcus
